#! -rules CONF-08 -strict
# 7777 everywhere, reached through constants, a flag default, net.JoinHostPort and compose mappings with a
# host IP; other ports are not the gateway's (NATS, a trunk, a test's, TCP 8080); a commented-out mapping
# and a printf whose format names the gateway are not read, nor are names that only contain "port"
# (transport, report_interval).
# 7777 also through ipv4 with an octet array, ipv6, "host:" + port, fmt.Sprint, Port fields, a TOML inline
# table and quoted key, and an upper-case /UDP mapping.
# 7777 through host + ":" + port with a host variable and multi-line TOML arrays; an array of arrays whose
# element line looks like a table header.
# C++: the overloads' ports on read lines, std::string{"host:"} + port, `<< 7776 + 1`, and a split
# initializer and option default; statements after a read statement or a gateway #include are not read.
# YAML: an unquoted flow sequence.
# Go: gateway-typed literals at 7777, elided and with an address field.
# TOML: a supervised gateway's command line at 7777; another process's options with other ports, and a
# trailing --listen with no value.
# C++: a block's body starts a new statement (after `) const {`, `) {` and a namespace name), so its addresses
# are not read; an initializer split after its brace is read up to its end only; a parenthesis left open by
# preprocessor branches ends with its block, so the next statements are read apart.
# TOML: arrays of inline tables at 7777 after a triple-quoted string with a quote and a bracket.
# C++: names whose words are not listen or connect (trunkBind, connectedPeers) do not make a read line.
# Go: a port operand in parentheses (concat.go).
# C++ brace forms whose braces open blocks (gateway_braces.cpp). TOML: a nested array of inline tables and a
# gateway table's command line at 7777.
